claims.explanation: Mocetinostat is a class I HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on HDAC1/2/3-mediated epigenetic programs rather than by a single lineage. The strongest pattern is that sensitive lines frequently carry TP53 pathway alterations together with activating PI3K/MAPK or chromatin-remodeler mutations, whereas resistant lines are enriched for mesenchymal/EMT-like states and KRAS-driven pancreatic or mesothelioma models. High expression of class I HDACs or ZEB1/EMT programs is predicted to modulate response, with ZEB1-associated resistance reversible by mocetinostat.

features.basis: Most selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations, consistent with loss of p53-dependent survival upon HDAC inhibition
Recurrent in sensitive lines (KYSE70, HCC1954, T47D, HGC27, MKN1, SNU840), suggesting PI3K-pathway dependence
Mocetinostat targets HDAC1/2/3; higher class I HDAC expression predicts greater target engagement and dependency
Class I HDAC target of mocetinostat; expression marks tumors reliant on HDAC-mediated epigenetic silencing
Class I HDAC target of mocetinostat; expression marks tumors reliant on HDAC-mediated epigenetic silencing
ZEB1-driven EMT and stemness confer resistance that mocetinostat can reverse, so high ZEB1 predicts poor single-agent response
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and lung lines are enriched among least affected lines, suggesting KRAS-driven resistance
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines (KYSE70, T47D, EFE184, LOXIMVI), implicating SWI/SNF loss in HDAC-inhibitor sensitivity
BRAF-mutant melanoma and thyroid lines (WM793, IGR37, 8305C) are among sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant lung/esophageal lines (NCIH1650, KYSE70) are selectively killed
NF2-mutant mesothelioma and thyroid sarcoma lines are among least affected, suggesting NF2 loss protects
CDKN2A deletions appear in several resistant lines (8305C, SUIT2, YD10B, MHHES1), though also in sensitive 8305C
